approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh surplus of molecular graphs from its highest-scoring accepted survivors, using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learns from all accepted observations, and correlated posterior draws select each evaluation batch. Accepted offspring compete for later breeding. Before pool admission, the Parent confirms that each canonical molecular identity is stable, normalizing verified aliases and rejecting unresolved representations. Its bond-change operator alters one existing bond order; it has no direct move that changes a ketone position while retaining the surrounding carbon skeleton.
approach.novelty: Add a ketone-position move that transfers a terminal carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene carbon. Both the old and new carbonyl must have carbon neighbors, so the move retains the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class while changing the oxygen position. It becomes an alternative within the existing bond-change operator. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms, exchanged aromatic nitrogen positions or moved branches around aromatic rings. This experiment instead offers a coordinated positional change within a saturated carbon framework.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-213e85380e04 completes its supplied panel with macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and population SD 0.013310111166991866, but only 565 of 4350 accepted offspring beat their best generating parent. Its identity-admission mechanism leaves every evaluated molecule and score unchanged from its own Parent. The molecular assessment identifies limited alternatives around recurring aromatic/carbonyl arrangements, while the actual change_bond implementation only changes one existing bond order. It cannot perform the registered two-bond oxygen reattachment in one local operation. A read-only audit of the Parent's fifteen saved task logs finds the exact eligible ketone/methylene rule in 137 of 4350 emitted graphs, with 145 site options, and in the primary parent of 2097 of 75607 outer breeding attempts. Those repeated draws involve 60 distinct accepted primary-parent identities with 62 distinct source/site options. Among 738 attempts whose only realized operation is change_bond, 27 have an eligible source; the Parent logs do not identify the internal selected bond, so this does not count actual selections of an eligible site. Unscored construction on the 145 emitted-source options and 62 distinct breeding-parent options yields source-distinct, parse/serialize-stable products with unchanged formula and atom/bond counts in every case. This is a feasibility and opportunity audit, not a new trajectory, global-novelty result or oracle comparison. The carbonyl-protection sibling n-9bee44b1c9c3 preserved C=O endpoints yet changed adjacent functional relationships and lost 0.034753 in paired macro mean. The nitrogen-position sibling n-9edaa26007c3 supplies one directly observed incumbent gain from a positional edit, whereas the aromatic-branch sibling n-2bb53b5f7b44 shows that intact positional alternatives can activate without meeting their score target. These observations motivate access to a specific new ketone neighborhood, without assuming that carbonyl retention or positional changes are intrinsically beneficial.
hypothesis: Offer direct transfer of a ketone carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene as an alternative within change_bond, preserving molecular formula, the carbon skeleton and ketone class while exposing a new carbonyl position to the inherited fresh-pool selector.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and crowded amines retain reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The observed output contains substantial aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry: compact bridged aryl carbonyls, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, halogenated polyamines, larger aza rings, and fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure text rates span 0.9782–0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates span 0.9471–0.9897; these are proportions of proposal strings containing the corresponding feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Functional-group diversity and differing core families justify moderate overall structural diversity, but the highest-scoring excerpts repeatedly modify related cores. Familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N–halogen, O–halogen and peroxide bonds, crowded aminals, unusual bridges, and very large repeated assemblies, making overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. No proposal string specifies an atom stereocentre or formal charge. Neutral strings do not imply absence of potentially basic amines. All five objectives have supplied trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The observed deco_hop seed-2 trajectory stops at evaluation 240, so its chemistry and comparisons with a parent trajectory reaching 300 describe partial coverage. Other supplied child task/seed trajectories reach 300. All child and parent trajectory files were read. Structural counts were derived passively with RDKit from those recorded molecules and are reproducible in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0010-15-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json. No new molecule, score, objective requirement or mechanism-activation judgment is introduced. Score gradients below are associations within the observed search histories, not isolated causal effects or claims of experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact aromatic carbonyl assemblies with densely bridged nitrogen-containing cores, small alkyl/alkoxy groups and fluorinated aromatic appendages. Proposal median size is 25 heavy atoms, the same as the parent; mean SMILES length is 45.0, ring-closure presence 0.9805 and aromatic presence 0.9793. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms, a bridged aza core and an N-fluoro carboxanilide. Other high excerpts retain an aroyl ketone or thioester; later products include fused N–N and N–O rings. The conventional methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilide in the initial set gives way to more demanding bridged structures. The parent leading family was also a compact bridged aryl/heteroaryl ketone, with recorded best 0.4463521672202675; the child leading N-fluoro amide reaches 0.4478476056206344. This is a change within a similar chemical region, with additional N–halogen occurrences: 243 of 870 proposals versus 187 of 870 in the parent.
liabilities: The leading amide has an N–F bond rather than an ordinary N–H or N–alkyl substituent. High numerical score does not establish its stability or suitability as a medicinal compound.

Thioesters, late N–N/N–O rings and short bridged connections need specific synthesis and stability assessment. The generated series does not specify configurations where potential atom stereocentres arise.
missing_features: The smallest low-scoring fragments omit the connected aromatic, nitrogen-containing core and carbonyl-bearing appendage shared by the stronger examples.

The stronger excerpts provide limited ordinary alternative core geometries that preserve this compact functional arrangement. Broader comparable amide/ketone structures without unusual N–F or bridged heteroatom connections remain underrepresented; an exact unseen preferred topology cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC scores 0.3051048083696145. The compact bridged N-fluoro amide CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1CN2C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 scores 0.4478476056206344, the aroyl ketone CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)Sc1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4238198477630873. Their shared aromatic/carbonyl assembly is compatible with the higher scores across different linker classes. The final N–N-ring/N-fluoro-amide product COc1cc2c(c(OC)c1CF)C=C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)NN2 scores 0.3630045684864706, whereas C=C and ClBr score 0.0. The upper score quartile contains 22–28 heavy atoms; lower-scoring proposals range from 1 to 49. This supports a coherent compact arrangement, without establishing that N–F, additional bridging or one carbonyl position independently improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpts join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatics through an NH linkage, with short annulated carbon bridges, aryl halogens, an aryl cyanate group and peroxide–halogen appendages. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms, but the entire observed proposal stream has median 52 and maximum 119 heavy atoms. Mean SMILES length is 114.4 and maximum 248; ring-closure and aromatic presence are both 0.9877. Late seed-2 molecules concatenate many N-alkylated dicarbonyl heterocycles and aromatic groups with ester, unsaturated and imine connections. The evaluation-235 example has 105 heavy atoms and 12 carbonyls. These are unusually large assemblies, even though many component functional groups are familiar. The parent proposal median was 45 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 94.4; its same leading linked-heteroaromatic molecule also scores 0.6324703199409752. The changed size distribution is descriptive because the child seed-2 trajectory is partial.
liabilities: O–O–Cl, O–O–F and O–halogen appendages are chemically reactive motifs. The aryl cyanate and short annulations add unresolved synthetic and stability questions.

Repeated polyaromatic/dicarbonyl assemblies carry a large synthetic burden and unmeasured solubility or conformational liabilities. Their continuing evaluation at substantial scores does not establish useful medicinal properties.
missing_features: The floor-score fragments lack the connected NH-linked aromatic acceptor arrangement carried by the stronger molecules.

High-scoring output gives few clearly tractable alternate implementations of that arrangement without unusual short annulations, cyanate or peroxide–halogen chemistry. The observed fluoromethyl variant shows that the O–O–halogen chain is already replaceable with little score change; broad stable alternatives are still limited.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 scores 0.548381482770623, compared with 0.6324703199409752 for Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(Br)cc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1. Methylamine CN scores the observed floor of 0.5. Within a closely related leading core, the peroxide–chlorine derivative Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(Br)nc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1 scores 0.6300605077662029, while the fluoromethyl alternative Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(CF)c5c(Br)nc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1 scores 0.6293992623616929. Replacing aryl bromine with methyl in Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(C)nc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1 retains 0.6300605077662029. The much larger evaluation-235 molecule scores 0.5920277939850422. The observed preference is compatible with linked carbonyl heteroaromatic features, while these reactive/halogen substituents and wholesale repetition have no demonstrated necessity.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products combine halogenated aromatic surfaces with several nonacyl amine centres, saturated or partly unsaturated aza rings and benzylic connections. One leading family has crowded aminals and linked diaza rings; another has sulfur–nitrogen polycycles with S=N/S–N bonds and an aryl O–Cl substituent. The strongest examples have 30–34 heavy atoms. Proposal median size is 34 heavy atoms versus 30 in the parent, with mean SMILES length 65.3, ring-closure presence 0.992, aromatic presence 0.9828 and halogen presence 0.992. The parent already had aryl-rich aminal and spiro-amine families; the child makes the sulfur–nitrogen family more prominent. Its observed best is 0.9846320606489212, while the parent observed best is 0.9914038363125457. Ring nitrogen availability is substantial: 834 of 870 child proposals contain a neutral, nonaromatic ring nitrogen with only single bonds and no adjacent carbonyl carbon. This structural flag is not a pKa prediction.
liabilities: Aryl O–Cl, congested aminal centres, low-valent sulfur–nitrogen connections and heavily halogenated aromatic groups make portions of the leading families less straightforward to synthesize and assess than their numerical scores suggest.

RDKit perceives potential unassigned atom stereocentres in 855 of 870 proposals, with no assigned atom stereocentres. These flags do not establish the number of isolable stereoisomers or their activity.
missing_features: The poor small aryl halide lacks the combined aromatic surface and spatially separated nonacyl amine centres seen in the stronger families; the acidic amide has different nitrogen electronics and connecting geometry.

The output lacks explicit configurations for its crowded amine and bridged cores, and supplies limited uncomplicated linkers that retain the high-scoring aryl/amine arrangement without aminal or unusual sulfur–nitrogen construction. A score benefit from specifying stereochemistry was not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur–nitrogen polycycle Nc1c(OCl)cccc1S1=NC2(C(F)c3cc(F)cc(Cl)c3)CCCN2C2CCN21 scores 0.9846320606489212 and the aryl/aminal/polyamine assembly CCc1cc(F)ccc1C(N)N(C)CC1CC=C(CC2N(C)CCN2c2cccc(Cl)c2Br)N1 0.9824209293387903. The small aromatic halide Fc1cccc(C(F)Cl)c1 scores 0.0009187819241663214, and the acidic amide COc1cc(F)cc(-c2ccc(C(CC(=O)O)NC(C)=O)cc2)c1 0.000719339566735797. Even the initial larger compound containing a ring amine scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so an amine by itself is insufficient. The visible gradient favors its combination and geometry with aromatic groups. In a closer comparison, the O–Cl-bearing polycycle Nc1c(OCl)cccc1S1=NC2(C(F)c3cc(F)cc(Cl)c3)CNCCN2C2CCN21 scores 0.9800122111448683 and the phenol Nc1c(O)cccc1S1=NC2(C(F)c3cc(F)cc(Cl)c3)CNCCN2C2CCN21 0.9783214156484753; the high score does not require the O–Cl liability. Upper-quartile size is 24–37 heavy atoms, while lower-quartile size extends to 80.

per_task.generated_character: The output consists mainly of medium-sized aromatic/aza-ring assemblies containing N-methylated amine and amidic centres, dicarbonyl groups, and alkyl-substituted aryl or quinoline-like appendages. Larger unsaturated aza rings and fused/bridged alternatives recur. The leading structures range from a 35-heavy-atom N-fluorinated polycycle to 28-heavy-atom quinoline-bearing larger rings. Proposal median size is 31 heavy atoms in both child and parent; mean SMILES length is 56.5, ring-closure presence 0.9966 and aromatic presence 0.9897. Halogen presence is 0.2816, so halogenation is less pervasive than in the other streams. Recognizable amides, ketones and amines are present, but their complete macrocyclic or bridged assembly remains synthetically demanding. The parent observed best was 0.22405709718343647, versus 0.2133697489012744 for this child, despite their similar broad chemical character and median size.
liabilities: The highest excerpt contains an N–F bond. O–halogen connections also occur in 152 of 870 proposed molecules, even though they are absent from several leading examples.

Complex larger-ring or bridged connections, unspecified configurations and unsaturated ring geometry require synthesis and conformational assessment. The low-scoring small cyclic peroxide is a distinct strained/reactive outlier, not representative of the dominant aromatic chemistry.
missing_features: The small low-scoring fragments lack the combined aromatic appendage, aza-ring geometry and dicarbonyl arrangement of the stronger compounds.

The stronger excerpts offer limited simple alternative ring connections that retain the same carbonyl and nonacyl-versus-amidic nitrogen relationships. Similar size and plentiful rings leave the relevant arrangement incompletely explored; no exact missing target substructure follows from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 scores 0.1678386594791329. The leading N-fluoro polycycle CCOc1ccc2c(N3CCN(F)C4C(=C3c3ccccc3C)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)CN4C)c1CO2 scores 0.2133697489012744, versus 0.2083446370599542 for CCOc1ccc2c(N3CCN(F)C4C(=C3c3ccccc3C)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)N4C)c1CO2, whose corresponding ring path lacks a methylene between carbonyl and nitrogen. Both ring size and amine/amidic context differ, so a single causal feature cannot be assigned. The halogen-free larger ring CC1=C(Cc2cc(O)nc3ccccc23)N(C)CCN(C)CC(=O)N(C)C1=O still scores 0.21037674112349405. Ethane CC scores 0.012461119656980673, and the small cyclic peroxide C1COO1 0.0239774717598468. A 41-heavy-atom final molecule with repeated quinoline-like appendages scores 0.1754730092490373. The stronger examples combine aromatic, aza-ring and dicarbonyl features; additional ring content, N–F or repeating the aromatic appendage is not established as necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family has a compact fluorinated aryl group bearing aminomethyl or aminoethyl substituents and an N-alkylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. The best molecule has 27 heavy atoms, a free primary amine and several carbon-bound fluorines, without an N–halogen bond. Neighboring high excerpts include N-fluorinated congeners. The changed seed-2 family instead has fused heteroaromatics, a fluorinated unsaturated amine ring, N–F, an N–S–methyl attachment and enol-bearing side chains. Proposal median size remains 27 heavy atoms as in the parent; mean SMILES length is 52.4, ring-closure presence 0.9782, aromatic presence 0.9471 and halogen presence 0.7724. Cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.0494, a minority feature. The same leading aminomethyl molecule scores 0.5845583988949146 in child and parent. The different seed-2 family reaches 0.49100694002536677, compared with the parent same-seed observed best 0.4071395189354175; this does not isolate the benefit of any one new group. N–halogen occurrences increase from 84 to 179 of 870 proposals.
liabilities: N-fluorination, N–S–methyl substitution, unsaturated small rings and enol substituents introduce stability, tautomer and synthetic questions in the alternate families. The leading aminomethyl structure is comparatively conventional.

Whole-core duplication creates large aromatic assemblies with extremely low recorded scores. Explicit stereochemical assignment remains absent where the changed ring products introduce potential atom stereocentres.
missing_features: The very bulky repeated cores and several late fused products omit the exposed pendant primary amine and specific fluorinated-aryl arrangement of the leading compact family, despite retaining carbonyl heterocycles.

There is limited coverage of alternative conventional carbonyl cores and amine attachment geometries at comparable size. Late ring-amine alternatives show some coverage, but retain unusual N–F/N–S chemistry; the trajectories do not establish an unseen objective-specific motif that would close the remaining score gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminomethyl compound Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc(CN)c(F)c(CF)c3CF)cc2n(CF)c1=O scores 0.5845583988949146. Its aryl-chloro analogue Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc(CN)c(F)c(CF)c3Cl)cc2n(CF)c1=O scores 0.5064928497454653, associating the changed fluoromethyl placement with improvement within this family. The N-fluoro aminoethyl congener CCc1c(F)c(CCN)cc(-n2cc3c(c2F)c(=O)n(F)c(=O)n3CF)c1F still scores 0.5652209810580261. The bulky repeated-core molecule Cn1c(=O)c2c(-c3ccccc3)n(-c3cc4cc(c3O)C(n3c(=O)c5c(-c6ccccc6)n(-c6cc(C(=O)OCCl)ccc6O)cc5n(C)c3=O)OC4=O)cc2n(C)c1=O has 60 heavy atoms and scores 1.6758614448245604e-53, while the initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298. The final fused series also spans 0.019466813955521963 for CSn1c(=O)c2c(C3=CCC3)n3c(c2n(F)c1=O)C(CF)C=C3C=CO to 0.4347774313557844 for CSn1c(=O)c2c(C3=CC(F)CN3)n3c(CC=CO)cccc3c2n(F)c1=O. Several groups and connections differ in that comparison. The upper score quartile contains 21–30 heavy atoms, favoring bounded combinations of substituents over duplication of whole cores. The primary-amine family is the clearest observed pattern, not a universal requirement for every useful molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The N-fluoro amide CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1CN2C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 scores 0.4478476056206344. The peroxide–chlorine derivative Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(Br)nc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1 scores 0.6300605077662029, while its fluoromethyl replacement Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(CF)c5c(Br)nc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1 scores 0.6293992623616929. The O–Cl-bearing polycycle Nc1c(OCl)cccc1S1=NC2(C(F)c3cc(F)cc(Cl)c3)CNCCN2C2CCN21 scores 0.9800122111448683, while its phenol Nc1c(O)cccc1S1=NC2(C(F)c3cc(F)cc(Cl)c3)CNCCN2C2CCN21 scores 0.9783214156484753. These observed alternatives show that high scores can coexist with more conventional substituents and do not make reactive bonds a requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional functional-group chemistry while exploring productive aromatic and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically conventional substituent and linker alternatives that preserve the surrounding aromatic, donor, acceptor or amine arrangement. Track functional-group class and reactive bond formation separately from parse validity and observed score, and let feedback determine utility without a hidden objective template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An observed proposal stream has mean SMILES length 114.4 and maximum 248. Its evaluation-235 repeated heterocyclic assembly C=CC(N=C)n1c(=O)n(C)c(=O)c2c(C(C)=O)n(-c3cc(OC(=O)C=CC(=C(C=Cn4c(=O)n(C)c(=O)c5c(C)n(-c6cc(C(=O)Oc7ccc(C(=O)C#N)cc7-n7cc8c(c7N(C=C)CF)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n8C)c(Cl)cc6OC)nc54)OC)n4nc5c(c4C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n5C)c4cc3C4)nc21 has 105 heavy atoms and score 0.5920277939850422, while its leading 32-heavy-atom compound scores 0.6324703199409752. Elsewhere Cn1c(=O)c2c(-c3ccccc3)n(-c3cc4cc(c3O)C(n3c(=O)c5c(-c6ccccc6)n(-c6cc(C(=O)OCCl)ccc6O)cc5n(C)c3=O)OC4=O)cc2n(C)c1=O has 60 heavy atoms and score 1.6758614448245604e-53, and C=C scores 0.0. Both uncontrolled repetition and severe fragmentation occur. These histories do not establish one universal preferred size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain a coherent molecular size when changing connected functional arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bounded local or scaffold changes that preserve a connected set of useful functional features without duplicating entire aromatic assemblies or discarding most of a molecule. Use structural context and observed feedback rather than a fixed task-specific molecular-size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest task has stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0. Passive graph perception finds potential unassigned atom stereocentres in 855 of 870 proposals in the most amine-rich stream, with no assigned atom stereocentres. CCc1cc(F)ccc1C(N)N(C)CC1CC=C(CC2N(C)CCN2c2cccc(Cl)c2Br)N1 contains crowded aminal and ring centres but no stereochemical tags. This establishes absent representation coverage, not that every perceived centre gives stable isolable stereoisomers or that charge is chemically absent.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks systematic stereochemical specification for the nonplanar ring and amine structures it produces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configuration-preserving and configuration-varying proposals at chemically meaningful stereogenic centres, including consistent representation when ring topology changes. Treat configurations as observed molecular alternatives with the same task-agnostic feedback, without assuming an unmeasured score advantage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading polycycle CCOc1ccc2c(N3CCN(F)C4C(=C3c3ccccc3C)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)CN4C)c1CO2 scores 0.2133697489012744 versus 0.2083446370599542 for CCOc1ccc2c(N3CCN(F)C4C(=C3c3ccccc3C)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)N4C)c1CO2, where the corresponding carbonyl-to-nitrogen ring path lacks a methylene. Both ring geometry and nitrogen electronics change. The halogen-free larger ring CC1=C(Cc2cc(O)nc3ccccc23)N(C)CCN(C)CC(=O)N(C)C1=O scores 0.21037674112349405. Other strong excerpts already contain multiple ring amines, so a blanket lack of nitrogen or rings is contradicted by the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful amine and carbonyl arrangements recur within related cores, with limited ordinary alternatives that preserve their electronic relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer alternative accessible ring connections and functional-group placements while preserving selected donor, acceptor and nonacyl-amine relationships. Expose deliberate changes of amine versus amide character separately enough for feedback to distinguish them; additional ring closures or unique strings alone do not establish useful chemical coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The compact aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl compound Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc(CN)c(F)c(CF)c3CF)cc2n(CF)c1=O scores 0.5845583988949146, and its aryl-chloro analogue Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc(CN)c(F)c(CF)c3Cl)cc2n(CF)c1=O 0.5064928497454653. The alternate fused product CSn1c(=O)c2c(C3=CCC3)n3c(c2n(F)c1=O)C(CF)C=C3C=CO retains dicarbonyl chemistry but lacks that pendant amine arrangement and scores 0.019466813955521963; a different ring-amine product CSn1c(=O)c2c(C3=CC(F)CN3)n3c(CC=CO)cccc3c2n(F)c1=O scores 0.4347774313557844. These are combined-context differences, not evidence that adding one amine universally helps.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently carry combined aromatic substitution and accessible amine features into its alternative carbonyl cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Create alternative core or attachment geometries that can retain an accessible amine and aromatic substitution context together with intact carbonyl functionality. Let the same observed-feedback process discover which combinations matter across objectives, without inserting a benchmark molecule or required task-specific pharmacophore.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
